svg.aria-label: Diagram: what the new Amazon ECS deployment timeline surfaces and the circuit breaker mechanics behind it. The console timeline narrates a deployment as it happens and carries four signals: circuit breaker status with live task failure and threshold tracking, deployment alarm state, container and load-balancer health checks, and lifecycle hook status. Below that, the circuit breaker's two stages are shown. Stage one monitors whether tasks reach the RUNNING state, and a task that fails to do so increases the failure count. Stage two begins once at least one task is running and checks health against Elastic Load Balancing, AWS Cloud Map and Amazon ECS container health checks, with each failure also increasing the count. When the failure count equals the threshold the deployment is marked FAILED and launches no new tasks. The threshold itself is calculated by the default BOUNDED_PERCENT type, which multiplies a value defaulting to 50 by the latest desired task count and clamps the result between a minimum of three and a maximum of 200, so a desired count of one still tolerates three failures, a desired count of 25 gives 13, and a desired count of 400 or 800 gives 200. A panel records the rollback trap: rollback targets the most recent COMPLETED deployment, and starting the rollback moves that deployment to IN_PROGRESS so it is no longer eligible as a rollback target, meaning that if a following deployment also fails with no COMPLETED deployment behind it the circuit breaker launches no new tasks and the deployment stalls. A final note records that the console view shortens diagnosis while AWS still recommends an EventBridge rule on SERVICE_DEPLOYMENT_FAILED for anything automated.
svg.title: A timeline for the human, an EventBridge rule for the pipeline
svg.text: Four signals that already existed, finally on one clock
The timeline narrates the deployment. It does not decide anything.
The new console timeline — Linear, Canary, Blue/Green
circuit breaker status · deployment alarm state · container and load-balancer health checks · lifecycle hook status
All Regions and GovCloud (US) · no charge · nothing to enable
Stage 1 · does the task start?
Watches for tasks reaching RUNNING.
A task that never gets there:
failure count + 1
Stage 2 · is it healthy?
Checks ELB, AWS Cloud Map and ECS
container health checks.
failure count + 1
The threshold nobody set — BOUNDED_PERCENT, default value 50
min 3 ≤ (value / 100) × desired task count ≤ max 200
desired 1 → 3
desired 25 → 13
desired 400 → 200
a large service tolerates 200 failed tasks
The rollback trap
Rollback targets the most recent COMPLETED deployment — and starting the rollback moves it to IN_PROGRESS,
so it is no longer eligible as a target. If the next deployment also fails, there is nothing COMPLETED behind it.
“The circuit breaker does not launch new tasks and the deployment is stalled.”
resetOnHealthyTask defaults to true — only consecutive failures count, so an intermittently-failing deployment may never trip the breaker.
For anything automated, AWS still recommends an EventBridge rule on SERVICE_DEPLOYMENT_FAILED. A timeline is not a rollback mechanism.
